html:
Hungary is a country in the Carpathian Basin, on the middle Danube. The map shows the medieval kingdom from 1100 to 1300, filling the whole basin, and the much smaller modern state from 1920 to 2010.

The Magyars settled the basin around 895. Their prince Stephen I was crowned king in 1000 and made the country Christian; his Árpád dynasty ruled until 1301. Croatia joined the crown in 1102. In 1222 nobles forced the king to grant the Golden Bull, a charter of their rights.

The Mongol invasion of 1241 laid the kingdom waste, and King Béla IV rebuilt it with stone castles. Under Matthias Corvinus, from 1458 to 1490, Buda had one of the first Renaissance courts north of the Alps.

At the Battle of Mohács in 1526 the Ottomans killed the king, and Hungary split in three: the Habsburg strip of Royal Hungary, the Ottoman centre and a Transylvanian principality. The Habsburgs retook the whole by 1699. Hungarians rose against them in 1848 and lost, but in 1867 won equal partnership in Austria-Hungary.

After the First World War the Treaty of Trianon of 1920 took away about two thirds of the old kingdom, which is why the 1920 map is so much smaller. Hungary fought beside Germany in the Second World War and then came under Soviet control. The revolution of 1956 was crushed by Soviet tanks. Communist rule ended in 1989, and Hungary joined the European Union in 2004.
sum: Hungary is a country in the Carpathian Basin, on the middle Danube. The map shows the medieval kingdom from 1100 to 1300, filling the whole basin, and the much smaller modern state from 1920 to 2010.
